chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us who said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abi al-Jarud, from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari who said:

I entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her) and in front of her was a tablet upon which were inscribed the names of the Trustees. I counted twelve, one of them being the Riser (al-Qa'im). Three of them were named Muhammad and three of them were named Ali.

key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: The Trustees or Successors, referring to the Imams
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Riser, a title for the twelfth Imam
key_terms.فَاطِمَةَ: Fatimah al-Zahra, the daughter of the Prophet
key_terms.لَوْحٌ: A tablet or board, here referring to a physical object inscribed with names

ai.seo_question: What are the names of the twelve Trustees listed on the tablet seen by Jabir ibn Abdullah in the presence of Fatimah?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* underscores the Fatimid lineage of the Imams, emphasizing that the twelve Trustees are directly descended from the Prophet through his daughter Fatimah and son-in-law Ali. The specific mention of three 'Muhammads' and three 'Alis' highlights the dual prominence of the Prophet and the First Imam within the Imamate, while identifying the twelfth as al-Qa'im, linking the chain of authority to the eventual Mahdi. This serves as a key textual proof for the number and identity of the Imams in Shia theology, rooted in the Ahl al-Bayt's own testimony.
